exercises.prompt: The witness ___ that she had seen the suspect.
exercises.answer: said
acceptedAnswers: said
exercises.hint: Il n'y a pas de personne juste après le verbe.
exercises.explanation: Say se construit sans personne : said that… Tell demande toujours la personne juste après (told the police that…). Ici il n'y a pas de personne : said.

extraExample.text: He said that he was tired.
extraExample.translation: Il a dit qu'il était fatigué.

errorPatterns.feedback: Tell doit être suivi de la personne (told the police, told me). Sans personne : said.
Speak ne s'utilise pas pour rapporter des paroles avec that : said that…
Talk ne s'utilise pas pour rapporter des paroles avec that : said that…

exercises.instruction: Associe chaque mot anglais à sa traduction.
exercises.prompt: Les mots de l'enquête
exercises.answer: witness = témoin ; police = police ; suspect = suspect ; crime = délit, crime ; guilty = coupable
exercises.explanation: The police est suivi d'un verbe au pluriel (the police are). Crime désigne aussi la criminalité en général (crime is rising). Dans guilty, le u est muet : /ˈɡɪlti/.
exercises.tip: The police are… : toujours le pluriel.

extraExample.text: The police are looking for two suspects.
extraExample.translation: La police recherche deux suspects.

exercises.prompt: « I will call you tomorrow, » said Tom. → Tom said he ___ call me the next day.
exercises.answer: would
acceptedAnswers: would
exercises.explanation: Après said (au passé), will recule en would : Tom said he would call me. Tomorrow devient the next day.

extraExample.text: She said she would help us.
extraExample.translation: Elle a dit qu'elle nous aiderait.

errorPatterns.feedback: Après said, le temps recule d'un cran : will → would.
Could est le recul de can. Le recul de will est would.
Did ne s'emploie pas ici : will → would.

exercises.prompt: The suspect claimed that he ___ at home all evening.
exercises.context: « I was at home all evening. »
exercises.answer: had been
acceptedAnswers: had been
was
exercises.explanation: Claimed est au passé : le temps recule d'un cran. Le past simple (was) devient souvent le past perfect (had been). À l'oral, on garde aussi was.
exercises.tip: Past simple → past perfect après said / claimed.

extraExample.text: She said she had finished the report.
extraExample.translation: Elle a dit qu'elle avait terminé le rapport.

errorPatterns.feedback: Has been est au présent : après claimed (passé), les temps reculent, donc had been.
Après claimed (passé), le temps recule : la phrase d'origine est au passé, donc had been (ou was).
Will be est un futur ; la phrase d'origine est au passé : had been.

exercises.prompt: Last week, Anna told me that she would see me ___.
exercises.context: « I'll see you tomorrow, » Anna told me last week.
exercises.answer: the next day
acceptedAnswers: the next day
the following day
exercises.hint: On rapporte la phrase une semaine plus tard.
exercises.explanation: Quand on rapporte les paroles plus tard, les repères de temps changent : tomorrow devient the next day (ou the following day). Tomorrow ne convient que si on rapporte le jour même.
exercises.tip: tomorrow → the next day ; yesterday → the day before ; today → that day.

extraExample.text: He said he had called me the day before.
extraExample.translation: Il a dit qu'il m'avait appelé la veille.

errorPatterns.feedback: Une semaine plus tard, « demain » n'est plus le même jour : tomorrow devient the next day.
The day before = la veille. Tomorrow devient the next day (le lendemain).
Yesterday = hier ; ici il s'agit du lendemain : the next day.

exercises.prompt: What did the suspect say to the police?
exercises.context: A man was questioned yesterday after a robbery at a jewellery shop. A witness told the police that she had seen two men running away. The suspect admitted that he had been in the street, but he denied that he had taken anything. He said that he would help the police.
options: He had been in the street but hadn't taken anything.
He had seen two men running away.
He had taken the jewellery but wanted to help.
He had never been in that street.
exercises.answer: He had been in the street but hadn't taken anything.
acceptedAnswers: He had been in the street but hadn't taken anything.
exercises.explanation: Le suspect a admis qu'il était dans la rue (admitted that he had been in the street), mais il a nié avoir pris quoi que ce soit (denied that he had taken anything). C'est le témoin qui avait vu deux hommes s'enfuir.

extraExample.text: She admitted that she had made a mistake.
extraExample.translation: Elle a admis qu'elle avait fait une erreur.

errorPatterns.equals: he had seen two men running away
errorPatterns.feedback: C'est le témoin (a witness) qui a vu deux hommes s'enfuir, pas le suspect.

errorPatterns.equals: he had taken the jewellery but wanted to help
errorPatterns.feedback: Le suspect a nié avoir pris quoi que ce soit (denied that he had taken anything).

errorPatterns.equals: he had never been in that street
errorPatterns.feedback: Il a admis (admitted) qu'il était dans la rue.

exercises.instruction: Complète avec le verbe find au passif.
exercises.prompt: The stolen car ___ by the police near the station yesterday.
exercises.answer: was found
acceptedAnswers: was found
exercises.hint: La voiture subit l'action, et c'était hier.
exercises.explanation: La voiture subit l'action (la police l'a trouvée) : c'est un passif. Yesterday est dans le passé et the stolen car est singulier : was found (find – found – found).
exercises.tip: Find – found – found : au passif, was found.

extraExample.text: The missing child was found safe.
extraExample.translation: L'enfant disparu a été retrouvé sain et sauf.

errorPatterns.feedback: Sans was, la phrase devient active : la voiture aurait trouvé quelque chose. Au passif : was found.
Yesterday est dans le passé : was found.
The stolen car est singulier : was found.

exercises.prompt: Le témoin a dit à la police qu'elle n'avait rien vu.
exercises.answer: The witness told the police that she hadn't seen anything.
acceptedAnswers: The witness told the police that she hadn't seen anything.
The witness told the police that she had not seen anything.
The witness told the police that she had seen nothing.
The witness told the police that she didn't see anything.
The witness told the police that she saw nothing.
The witness told the police she hadn't seen anything.
The witness told the police she had not seen anything.
The witness told the police she had seen nothing.
The witness told the police she didn't see anything.
The witness told the police she saw nothing.
The witness said to the police that she hadn't seen anything.
The witness said to the police that she had not seen anything.
The witness said to the police that she had seen nothing.
The witness said to the police that she didn't see anything.
The witness said to the police that she saw nothing.
The witness said to the police she hadn't seen anything.
The witness said to the police she had not seen anything.
The witness said to the police she had seen nothing.
The witness said to the police she didn't see anything.
The witness said to the police she saw nothing.
exercises.hint: Tell est suivi de la personne.
exercises.explanation: Tell est toujours suivi de la personne (told the police) ; avec said, il faudrait to (said to the police). « N'avait rien vu » est un plus-que-parfait : hadn't seen anything.

extraExample.text: The officer told the driver that he had been speeding.
extraExample.translation: Le policier a dit au conducteur qu'il avait fait un excès de vitesse.

errorPatterns.feedback: Say ne prend pas directement la personne : told the police (ou said to the police).
Tell est toujours suivi de la personne : told the police that…
Après had, il faut le participe passé : seen (see – saw – seen).
Après hadn't, il faut le participe passé : seen (see – saw – seen).

exercises.prompt: Yesterday the police ___ two suspects, and today they are looking for a third one.
exercises.answer: questioned
acceptedAnswers: questioned
exercises.explanation: Yesterday indique un moment précis du passé : on utilise le past simple (questioned). Le present perfect (have questioned) ne s'emploie pas avec yesterday.
exercises.tip: Yesterday / last week / in 2019 → past simple.

extraExample.text: Last night the police closed the road.
extraExample.translation: Hier soir, la police a fermé la route.

errorPatterns.feedback: Pour un fait passé daté (yesterday), il faut le past simple : questioned.
Are questioning est au présent continu. Yesterday appelle le past simple : questioned.
Le present perfect ne s'emploie pas avec yesterday : past simple, questioned.

exercises.prompt: The man said that he ___ guilty.
exercises.answer: wasn't
acceptedAnswers: wasn't
was not
exercises.explanation: Said est au passé : le présent (I am not) recule au past simple (he was not). Am, is et are deviennent was ou were.
exercises.tip: am / is / are → was / were après said.

extraExample.text: She said she was ready.
extraExample.translation: Elle a dit qu'elle était prête.

errorPatterns.feedback: Après said (passé), le présent recule au passé : wasn't.
Won't be est un futur. « I'm not » est au présent : wasn't.
Hasn't been est un present perfect. « I'm not » est au présent : wasn't.

exercises.instruction: Remets les mots dans l'ordre pour traduire.
exercises.prompt: La police a dit qu'elle reviendrait le lendemain.
exercises.answer: The police said they would come back the next day
acceptedAnswers: The police said they would come back the next day
exercises.explanation: Said est directement suivi de la phrase rapportée (that est facultatif). Will recule en would, et « le lendemain » se dit the next day. The police est pluriel : they.

extraExample.text: They said they would call back the following week.
extraExample.translation: Ils ont dit qu'ils rappelleraient la semaine suivante.

exercises.instruction: Associe chaque phrase directe à sa version rapportée.
exercises.prompt: Du direct au rapporté

pairs.right: She said she would help me.
She said she had to go.

exercises.answer: « I am tired. » = She said she was tired. ; « I will help you. » = She said she would help me. ; « I can swim. » = She said she could swim. ; « I have finished. » = She said she had finished. ; « I must go. » = She said she had to go.
exercises.explanation: Le temps recule d'un cran : am → was, will → would, can → could, have finished → had finished, must → had to. Le pronom change aussi (I → she, you → me).
exercises.tip: Après said : am → was, will → would, can → could, have → had, must → had to.

extraExample.text: « I live here. » → He said he lived there.
extraExample.translation: « J'habite ici. » → Il a dit qu'il habitait là.

exercises.prompt: Il prétend qu'il n'a rien fait.
exercises.answer: He claims that he hasn't done anything.
acceptedAnswers: He claims that he hasn't done anything.
He claims that he has not done anything.
He claims that he didn't do anything.
He claims that he did not do anything.
He claims that he has done nothing.
He claims that he did nothing.
He claims he hasn't done anything.
He claims he has not done anything.
He claims he didn't do anything.
He claims he did not do anything.
He claims he has done nothing.
He claims he did nothing.
exercises.explanation: Prétend est au présent (claims) : le temps ne recule pas. Le recul n'a lieu que si le verbe d'introduction est au passé (claimed, said…). Claim = affirmer sans preuve.
exercises.tip: Verbe d'introduction au présent → pas de recul du temps.

extraExample.text: She says she is tired.
extraExample.translation: Elle dit qu'elle est fatiguée.

errorPatterns.feedback: Avec he, le verbe prend un -s : claims.
Claims est au présent : pas de recul du temps. On garde hasn't done (ou didn't do).
Claims est au présent : pas de recul du temps. On garde hasn't done (ou didn't do).

exercises.instruction: Remets les mots dans l'ordre pour traduire.
exercises.prompt: Le suspect a nié qu'il avait volé l'argent.
exercises.answer: The suspect denied that he had stolen the money
acceptedAnswers: The suspect denied that he had stolen the money
exercises.explanation: Deny that est suivi d'une proposition dont le temps recule : he stole → he had stolen. Steal – stole – stolen.
exercises.tip: Deny that + sujet + had + participe passé.

extraExample.text: She denied that she had broken the window.
extraExample.translation: Elle a nié avoir cassé la fenêtre.

exercises.prompt: The suspect denied everything and said that he had never seen the man.
exercises.answer: Le suspect a tout nié et a dit qu'il n'avait jamais vu cet homme.
acceptedAnswers: Le suspect a tout nié et a dit qu'il n'avait jamais vu cet homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a dit qu'il n'avait jamais vu l'homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a dit qu'il n'avait jamais vu ce monsieur.
Le suspect a tout nié et a affirmé qu'il n'avait jamais vu cet homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a affirmé qu'il n'avait jamais vu l'homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a affirmé qu'il n'avait jamais vu ce monsieur.
Le suspect a tout nié en disant qu'il n'avait jamais vu cet homme.
Le suspect a tout nié en disant qu'il n'avait jamais vu l'homme.
Le suspect a tout nié en disant qu'il n'avait jamais vu ce monsieur.
Le suspect a tout nié et a déclaré qu'il n'avait jamais vu cet homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a déclaré qu'il n'avait jamais vu l'homme.
Le suspect a tout nié et a déclaré qu'il n'avait jamais vu ce monsieur.
exercises.explanation: Denied everything = a tout nié. Had never seen est un plus-que-parfait : « n'avait jamais vu ». The man se traduit par « l'homme » ou « cet homme ».

extraExample.text: She said she had never been to London.
extraExample.translation: Elle a dit qu'elle n'était jamais allée à Londres.

exercises.prompt: The police officer ___ us that the street was closed.
exercises.answer: told
acceptedAnswers: told
exercises.hint: Il y a une personne (us) juste après.
exercises.explanation: Tell est toujours suivi de la personne (told us). Said ne peut pas être suivi directement de us : il faudrait said to us that…

extraExample.text: She told me that she was leaving.
extraExample.translation: Elle m'a dit qu'elle partait.

errorPatterns.feedback: Said ne prend pas directement la personne : told us that… ou said to us that…
Speak ne s'utilise pas pour rapporter des paroles avec that : told us that…
Talk ne s'utilise pas pour rapporter des paroles avec that : told us that…

exercises.prompt: Le témoin, qui a vu le suspect, habite près de la banque.
exercises.answer: The witness, who saw the suspect, lives near the bank.
acceptedAnswers: The witness, who saw the suspect, lives near the bank.
The witness, who saw the suspect, lives close to the bank.
The witness, who has seen the suspect, lives near the bank.
The witness, who has seen the suspect, lives close to the bank.
exercises.hint: Détail entre virgules sur une personne : who.
exercises.explanation: La relative « qui a vu le suspect » donne un détail sur un témoin déjà identifié : elle est entre virgules, avec who. Lives prend un -s (3e personne du singulier).

extraExample.text: Her husband, who works in a bank, travels a lot.
extraExample.translation: Son mari, qui travaille dans une banque, voyage beaucoup.

errorPatterns.feedback: Après une virgule, that est interdit : who.
Which ne s'utilise pas pour une personne : who.
Avec the witness (3e personne), le verbe prend un -s : lives.

exercises.prompt: Elle a admis qu'elle avait menti à la police.
exercises.answer: She admitted that she had lied to the police.
acceptedAnswers: She admitted that she had lied to the police.
She admitted that she lied to the police.
She admitted she had lied to the police.
She admitted she lied to the police.
exercises.hint: Lie – lied – lied. Mentir à = lie to.
exercises.explanation: Admit that est suivi d'une proposition dont le temps recule : « avait menti » = had lied. Mentir à quelqu'un se dit lie to someone.

extraExample.text: He admitted that he had been late.
extraExample.translation: Il a admis qu'il avait été en retard.

errorPatterns.feedback: Mentir à quelqu'un se dit lie to : lied to the police.
Mentir à quelqu'un se dit lie to : lied to the police.
Après had, il faut le participe passé : lied.

exercises.prompt: Comment dit-on « Elle a dit qu'elle l'avait vu la veille » ?
exercises.answer: She said that she had seen him the day before.
acceptedAnswers: She said that she had seen him the day before.
She said that she had seen him the previous day.
She said she had seen him the day before.
She said she had seen him the previous day.
She told me that she had seen him the day before.
She told me that she had seen him the previous day.
She told me she had seen him the day before.
She told me she had seen him the previous day.
exercises.hint: Hier, vu depuis un autre jour, devient the day before.
exercises.explanation: Said est au passé : « l'avait vu » = had seen. La veille se dit the day before (ou the previous day) : yesterday ne convient que si on rapporte les paroles le jour même.

extraExample.text: He said he had arrived the day before.
extraExample.translation: Il a dit qu'il était arrivé la veille.

errorPatterns.feedback: Say ne prend pas directement la personne : She said that… ou She told me…
Tell est toujours suivi de la personne : She told me that…
Quand on rapporte après coup, yesterday devient the day before (la veille).

exercises.prompt: Pense à une phrase qu'un ami ou un collègue t'a dite récemment. Rapporte-la en anglais avec said ou told.
exercises.answer: My friend told me that she was moving to Spain.
acceptedAnswers: My friend told me that she was moving to Spain.
My boss said that the meeting would start at nine.
Anna told me she couldn't come the next day.
He said he was tired.
exercises.hint: Said (that) + phrase ; told + personne (that) + phrase, avec le temps qui recule.
exercises.explanation: Après said ou told (au passé), les temps reculent d'un cran : am → was, will → would, can → could. N'oublie pas que told est toujours suivi de la personne (told me), pas said.

extraExample.text: He told me he would call the next day.
extraExample.translation: Il m'a dit qu'il appellerait le lendemain.

errorPatterns.feedback: Say ne prend pas directement la personne : told me… ou said to me…
Tell est toujours suivi de la personne : told me that…
